title: Complexe de De Rham à puissance divisée [conférence de 1976 à l’IHÉS] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
The page belongs to a block (pp. 365-367) where Grothendieck reviews the classical mod p homology and cohomology of Eilenberg-MacLane spaces. This background seems to serve the divided-power de Rham / derived Sym discussion of the 1976 talk. The previous page lists the Cartan seminar, the bar/Eilenberg-Moore spectral sequence for K(F_p,n+1)=B K(F_p,n), and Serre's 1954 method. The next page develops the bar construction and the Eilenberg-Zilber algebra structure on B(A).

(1) Coalgebra structure on the Steenrod algebra A. For a cohomology operation P, the pullback along the multiplication gives (mu^*P)(xy) = sum P^i x . P^j y. By the Cartan formula this yields the coproduct Delta P^i = sum_{j+k=i} P^j (x) P^k.

(2) Milnor's description of the dual A_*. xi_j (j>=1) is dual to the admissible monomial P^{p^{j-1}}...P^p P^1 in the admissible basis. tau_j (j>=0) is dual to the analogous monomial ending in beta. Then A_* = Sym(xi_i) (x) Lambda(tau_j), with coproducts Delta xi_k = sum_i xi_{k-i}^{p^i} (x) xi_i and Delta tau_k = tau_k (x) 1 + sum_{i=0}^k xi_{k-i}^{p^i} (x) tau_i. 'p85' is presumably a page reference to a source.

(3) Cup-product pairings. A pairing A (x) B -> C of F_p-modules induces K(A,i) ^ K(B,j) -> K(C,i+j). For K(F_p,n) ^ K(F_p,m) -> K(F_p,n+m), the induced map H^*K(F_p,n+m) -> H^*K(F_p,n) (x) H^*K(F_p,m) sends theta(iota) to the sum of theta'(iota) (x) theta''(iota). Stably this is the comultiplication of A, i.e. the dual of the multiplication of A_*.

(4) Left column: derived functors (Dold-Puppe) of Sym applied to the simplicial F_p-vector spaces K(F_p,n). The claims are:
- Stable L Sym^r = 0 unless r = p^s.
- There is a suspension map L_i Sym^s K(F_p,n) -> L_{i+1} Sym^s K(F_p,n+1).
- 'L^st_* Sym F_p = A_*', with Sym circled, followed by 'L^st_* F_p[F_p] ='. This is the stable derived functor of the group-algebra functor, which by Dold-Thom/Cartan gives lim H_{*+n}(K(F_p,n);F_p) = A_*.
- xi_1 and tau_0 are listed as living in weight p (Sym^p).

The purpose is to relate the weight filtration by Sym^d (or by powers of the augmentation ideal of F_p[V]) to the Milnor generators of A_*.
errors: tau_j is dual to P^{p^{j-1}}...P^p P^1 beta (degree 2p^j-1). The page writes the leading term as P^{p^j}, an index shift.

'L^st_* Sym F_p = A_*' is not correct for Sym over F_p. The stable derived functors of Sym_{F_p} are the stable operations on homotopy of simplicial commutative F_p-algebras (e.g. Dwyer's delta_i, i>=2, for p=2). Already in weight 2 these form an infinite-dimensional space, whereas the weight-2 part of A_* is finite. The circled 'Sym' and the immediate rewriting as 'L^st_* F_p[F_p]' suggest Grothendieck noticed this. With the group-algebra functor F_p[-] (or integral symmetric products with mod p homology, which gives H_*(HZ;F_p)) the identification is correct.
The suspension map is written L_i -> L_{n+i+1}; with consistent indexing it should be L_i Sym^s(V[n]) -> L_{i+1} Sym^s(V[n+1]).
'L Sym^r = 0 for r != p^s' only holds for stable derived functors (or mod p homology of symmetric-product quotients, Nakaoka), not unstably.

Milnor generators xi_j, tau_j of A_* and their coproduct formulas

ideas.modern_name: Multiplication on HF_p inducing the coalgebra structure

ideas.what: Stable derived functors of Sym^r vanish unless r=p^s; stable derived functors of the group-algebra/Sym functor give A_*, with xi_1, tau_0 in weight p
ideas.modern_name: Dold-Puppe stable derived functors; Nakaoka's symmetric products; Bousfield/Priddy/Dwyer operations on simplicial commutative algebras
ideas.usually_credited_to: Dold-Puppe, Nakaoka, Bousfield (1967), Priddy (1973), Dwyer (1980); used by Breen (1978)

missed.claim: Documents that in preparing the 1976 divided-power de Rham talk Grothendieck tied derived functors of Sym on K(F_p,n), with their weight filtration, to Milnor's generators of the dual Steenrod algebra. This parallels Breen's contemporaneous Ext(G_a,G_a) work. It is historical evidence of his engagement with the topic, not a new result.
missed.quote: L^{st}_* Sym F_p = A_* ... xi_1, tau_0 in Sym^p
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Historical context for derived de Rham/crystalline theory and the later Bhatt-style derived Sym/de Rham comparisons. The mathematics itself is known.

deep.surprise_reason: Standard review material (Milnor's dual Steenrod algebra, Cartan formula, Dold-Puppe stable derived functors), partly misstated. Mainly of historical interest as background to the 1976 talk.
transcription_corrections: tau_j line should read 'P^{p^j}...P^p P beta' as written by Grothendieck (itself an index slip), not with a dash as a minus sign.
'L^{st}_* [-F_p-] [F_p] =' is better read as 'L^{st}_* F_p[F_p] =', the stable derived functor of the group-algebra functor F_p[-].
In the cohomology-operation line the sum is Sum P^i x . P^j y (indices i, j as superscripts on P).
